The presence of necrosis (NCR Volume (mL) of 5.88) and significant contrast enhancement (ET Volume (mL) of 13.794) are classic imaging hallmarks of glioblastoma, which is the most common IDH-wildtype glioma. Additional features supporting an aggressive, wildtype tumor include significant mass effect (max_shift_mm of 7.0), deep gray matter involvement (thalamus, basal ganglia), and ependymal invasion. There are no significant features to suggest an IDH-mutant tumor.

Key features arguing against a 1p/19q co-deleted tumor (oligodendroglioma) include the presence of necrosis (Proportion Necrosis: 2.98%), a thick enhancing margin (>3mm), and extensive vasogenic edema (ED Volume (mL): 177.682). Oligodendrogliomas typically lack necrosis and have less prominent, if any, enhancement and edema. Deep gray matter involvement is also less common in oligodendrogliomas. Therefore, the tumor is almost certainly 1p/19q non-codeleted. This is also consistent with the high likelihood of IDH-wildtype status, as co-deletion is mutually exclusive with IDH-wildtype.

This finding alone is sufficient to assign grade 4. This is strongly corroborated by other features of high-grade malignancy, including the presence of contrast enhancement (ET Volume (mL) of 13.794), significant mass effect (max_shift_mm of 7.0), a large total tumor volume (197.356 mL), and ependymal invasion. overall_comment: The combination of advanced patient age (72) with imaging findings of a large, enhancing, and necrotic mass with significant mass effect is highly characteristic of Glioblastoma, IDH-wildtype, CNS WHO grade 4.
